title: Mara and the Thorn Revisited
premise: Ada Iversen, last apprentice of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that trades in impossible things—discovers her masters have been quietly selling souls to the court beneath the mountain to keep their dying dragon-fire lit. When a nameless child arrives speaking a language older than kingdoms, Ada learns he is the collateral on a debt her guild incurred generations ago, and that his soul is the next to be sold. To save him, she must steal back every soul in the mountain's ledger, including one belonging to her own grandmother, before the final flame gutters out and the court claims everything. In the end, Ada burns the guild's ledgers, frees the souls into the extinguished fire, and founds a new kind of guild—one with no debts, only members.
about_author: Quentin Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed estates and now writes fantasies about what we owe the dead. They live above a shuttered counting-house with two cats named after disputed inheritances.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unpaid Things
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She audits the guild's ledgers alone in a hall built for forty, tallying impossible inventory: bottled echoes, borrowed years, one sealed grief. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as diligence—she loves the ledger more than the guild that ignores her.

chapters.title: A Knock in a Dead Language
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A child of perhaps seven appears at the guild door at dusk, speaking a language no living tongue records—and the ledger opens itself to a page written in it. Ada hides him from the senior Keeper. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as she realizes the book knows him.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Deciphering the page, she finds a contract signed by the guild's founders: a soul held as collateral for a debt 'payable when the fire dims.' The child has no name because his name is listed as an asset. Beat: betrayal—the guild she worshipped traffics in people.

chapters.title: Keeper Vess Explains the Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The last senior Keeper admits everything with chilling calm: souls sold below keep the dragon-fire burning, and the fire keeps the world's borders standing. One more soul buys a century. Beat: seductive pragmatism—Vess genuinely believes she is saving the world.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The child dreams the guild's founding night in perfect detail, including the moment the first soul was taken. He begins calling Ada by her grandmother's name. Beat: tenderness and dread entwined—he is old in ways no child should be.

chapters.title: Downstairs, Where the Books Breathe
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She descends to the guild's sealed vault and finds the true ledger: a living book bound in something warm, listing thousands of names under the heading PAID IN FULL TO THE COURT BENEATH. Her grandmother's name is among them. Beat: grief becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Terms of Theft
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She resolves to steal the ledger's entries back, but the vault book warns: a debt unpaid can be transferred, not erased. Someone must go beneath the mountain. Beat: cold resolve—Ada volunteers herself as the new collateral if it comes to that.

chapters.title: The Last Honest Thief
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A disgraced guild thief, Bram owes Ada a life-debt from a job gone wrong. She recruits him; he laughs, then sees the vault book and stops laughing. Beat: reluctant alliance forged between two people the institution discarded.

chapters.title: Fire Is a Kind of Memory
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Researching dragon-fire, she learns it burns on remembered souls—that the court isn't imprisoning them but feeding memory itself to keep borders real. Freeing the souls may unravel the map. Beat: moral vertigo—rescue might cost the world its shape.

chapters.title: The Road That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The three travel toward the mountain through country where roads rearrange overnight, since fewer remembered souls hold fewer places in place. The child navigates by singing the dead language. Beat: fragile hope—the boy is a compass made of everything they're trying to free.

chapters.title: An Inn at the Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At an inn half-faded from existence, they meet a woman who sold her own sorrow decades ago and cannot remember why she cries. Ada shows her the vault book's copy of her entry. Beat: compassion sharpened into anger at the whole economy of souls.

chapters.title: Vess Follows
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The Keeper tracks them, not to stop them but to negotiate: return the child, and the guild will buy the others back slowly, over centuries. She reveals the fire is nearly out—weeks, not years. Beat: a ticking clock disguised as mercy.

chapters.title: The Gate of Paid Debts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They reach the mountain gate, carved with every contract ever honored. It opens only for someone listed in the ledger—Ada presents her own name, offered as surety. Beat: sacrifice accepted before it's demanded.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Below, a court of patient, courteous figures presides over shelves of sleeping flames, each holding a soul. The Magistrate is unfailingly polite and utterly immovable: contracts are sacred. Beat: horror of bureaucracy—evil as impeccable bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Flame
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds her grandmother's flame and speaks to the memory inside it; her grandmother tells her the founders' original sin—they stole the fire's first spark and have been paying interest in souls ever since. Beat: inheritance reframed as a debt she can refuse.

chapters.title: The Child's True Name
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Ada). The boy remembers his name at last—it was the first word of the dead language, meaning 'the one who is owed.' He is not collateral; he is the creditor. The entire court exists on credit extended to it by him. Beat: reversal—the smallest figure holds the largest claim.

chapters.title: Calling In the Debt
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Before the full court, the child speaks his claim in the old tongue; the Magistrate's composure cracks. But calling the debt due means the court must pay everything at once—including the fire that holds the world together. Beat: victory revealed as catastrophe unless someone finds a third option.

chapters.title: What Vess Carried Down
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Arriving mid-standoff, Vess does the unthinkable: she surrenders the guild's remaining assets, including her own long-held flame, to buy time. Beat: redemption through accounting—an enemy pays her own account in full.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The dragon-fire gutters; borders flicker; the inn-woman's village blinks out of memory around them. Ada makes her choice: feed the fire not souls but the ledgers themselves—all recorded debts, burned as fuel. Beat: climax—she destroys the guild's power to save everyone in it.

chapters.title: Ash and Release
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The flames take the ledgers and blaze brighter than ever, running now on forgiven debts. Souls rise as embers and scatter home. The court dissolves into quiet, almost grateful dust. Beat: catharsis—the world remade by cancellation, not payment.

chapters.title: A Guild With No Ledgers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, the guildhall reopens with a new sign: no debts kept here. The child, named at last, stays as its first member; Bram repairs the roof; Vess teaches history so it won't repeat. Beat: belonging earned, inheritance refused and replaced.

chapters.title: The First Blank Page
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the vault shelf sits the old living book, emptied and quiet, offering one blank page. Ada leaves it blank and locks the vault—not hiding it, just letting it rest. Final beat: peace as the discipline of not writing down what people owe.
